claim: Infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy (INAD) is caused by recessive variants in PLA2G6.
source: Infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy (INAD) (OMIM #256600) is a devastating and lethal pediatric neurodegenerative disorder caused by recessive variants in PLA2G6 (Khateeb et al., 2006; Morgan et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Khateeb et al., 2006 and Morgan et al., 2006

claim: INAD is a lethal pediatric neurodegenerative disorder.
source: Infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy (INAD) (OMIM #256600) is a devastating and lethal pediatric neurodegenerative disorder caused by recessive variants in PLA2G6 (Khateeb et al., 2006; Morgan et al., 2006).
evidence: Established clinical characterization of INAD

claim: Variants in PLA2G6 cause atypical NAD (aNAD).
source: Moreover, variants in PLA2G6 also cause atypical NAD (aNAD) (OMIM # 610217) and PLA2G6-related dystonia-parkinsonism, also called Parkinson disease 14 (PARK14) (OMIM #612953) (Paisan-Ruiz et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Paisan-Ruiz et al., 2009

claim: Variants in PLA2G6 cause PLA2G6-related dystonia-parkinsonism (PARK14).
source: Moreover, variants in PLA2G6 also cause atypical NAD (aNAD) (OMIM # 610217) and PLA2G6-related dystonia-parkinsonism, also called Parkinson disease 14 (PARK14) (OMIM #612953) (Paisan-Ruiz et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Paisan-Ruiz et al., 2009

claim: INAD, aNAD, and PARK14 are collectively called PLA2G6-associated neurodegeneration (PLAN).
source: Collectively, these three diseases are called PLA2G6-associated neurodegeneration (PLAN) (Kurian et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kurian et al., 2008

claim: Iron accumulation has been observed in the basal ganglia of some INAD, aNAD, and PARK14 patients.
source: Iron accumulation has been observed in the basal ganglia of some INAD and aNAD as well as PARK14 patients (Ferese et al., 2018; Yoshino et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ferese et al., 2018 and Yoshino et al., 2010

claim: PLAN diseases are categorized as neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation 2 (NBIA2).
source: Hence, these diseases are also categorized as neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation 2 (NBIA2) (OMIM #610217) (Gregory et al., 2008; Morgan et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gregory et al., 2008 and Morgan et al., 2006

claim: INAD symptoms include early onset ataxia at age 1-3 years.
source: The symptoms of INAD include early onset ataxia (age 1–3 years), mental and motor deterioration, hypotonia, progressive spastic tetraparesis, visual impairments, bulbar dysfunction, and extrapyramidal signs.
evidence: Clinical characterization of INAD symptoms

claim: INAD patients usually die before their 10th birthday.
source: INAD patients usually die before their 10th birthday.
evidence: Clinical observation of INAD prognosis

claim: aNAD and PARK14 patients have a later onset of symptoms compared to INAD.
source: In contrast to the severe defects in INAD, aNAD, and PARK14 patients have a later onset of symptoms, including progressive dystonia and parkinsonism.
evidence: Clinical comparison between disease presentations

claim: Cerebellar atrophy is a characteristic symptom in both INAD and aNAD.
source: Cerebellar atrophy is a characteristic symptom in both INAD and aNAD (Gregory et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gregory et al., 2008

claim: The formation of spheroid structures in the nervous system is a typical neuropathological hallmark of PLAN.
source: The formation of spheroid structures in the nervous system is a typical neuropathological hallmark of PLAN (Hedley-Whyte et al., 1968).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hedley-Whyte et al., 1968

claim: Spheroid structures in PLAN contain numerous membranes as well as α-synuclein and ubiquitin.
source: These spheroid structures contain numerous membranes as well as α-synuclein and ubiquitin (Riku et al., 2013) and are named tubulovesicular structures (TVSs) (Sumi-Akamaru et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Riku et al., 2013 and Sumi-Akamaru et al., 2015

claim: Lewy bodies and phosphorylated tau-positive neurofibrillary tangles have been observed in the nervous system of PLAN patients.
source: Moreover, Lewy bodies and phosphorylated tau-positive neurofibrillary tangles have also been observed in the nervous system of the PLAN patients (Paisán-Ruiz et al., 2012; Riku et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Paisán-Ruiz et al., 2012 and Riku et al., 2013

claim: Pla2g6KO/KO mice exhibit a normal lifespan.
source: Mice that lack Pla2g6 (genotype: Pla2g6KO/KO) exhibit a normal lifespan but show a slowly progressive motor defect, first observed at around 1 year of age (Malik et al., 2008; Shinzawa et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Malik et al., 2008 and Shinzawa et al., 2008

claim: Pla2g6KO/KO mice show a slowly progressive motor defect first observed at around 1 year of age.

evidence: Supported by citations to Malik et al., 2008 and Shinzawa et al., 2008

claim: Pla2g6KO/KO mice show progressive axonal degeneration.
source: These mice show some phenotypes observed in INAD patients, including a progressive axonal degeneration (Shinzawa et al., 2008), cerebellar atrophy (Zhao et al., 2011), and the presence of TVS and α-synuclein-containing spheroids in the nervous system (Malik et al., 2008; Shinzawa et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Shinzawa et al., 2008

claim: Pla2g6KO/KO mice show cerebellar atrophy.
source: These mice show some phenotypes observed in INAD patients, including a progressive axonal degeneration (Shinzawa et al., 2008), cerebellar atrophy (Zhao et al., 2011), and the presence of TVS and α-synuclein-containing spheroids in the nervous system (Malik et al., 2008; Shinzawa et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhao et al., 2011

claim: Pla2g6KO/KO mice show the presence of TVS and α-synuclein-containing spheroids in the nervous system.

claim: TEM revealed swelling of the presynaptic membrane, synaptic degeneration, and mitochondrial inner membrane defects in Pla2g6KO/KO mice.

claim: Homozygous Pla2g6G373R/G373R mice express Pla2g6-G373R protein at a comparable level to wild-type littermates.

claim: Pla2g6G373R/G373R mice show severe behavioral and neuropathological phenotypes at a much earlier age than Pla2g6KO/KO mice.

claim: No iron accumulation has been documented in the brain of both INAD mouse models.

claim: The sc-376563 antibody specifically recognizes endogenous PLA2G6.
source: We tested the specificity of three commercially available PLA2G6 antibodies and found one antibody that recognizes PAL2G6 (sc-376563 Santa Cruz Biotechnology; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-B). This antibody recognizes a band of the proper molecular weight in HEK-293T cells as well as induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and neural progenitor cells (NPCs) derived from a healthy person (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and Figure 1A). Moreover, this band was absent in HEK-293T cells that express PLA2G6 shRNAs and iPSCs and NPCs derived from an INAD patient with a PLA2G6-R70X variant (29-3; see below) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and Figure 1A). These data show that this antibody can specifically recognize endogenous PLA2G6.
evidence: Antibody validation experiments in multiple cell types
